ai.purpose: RTT/3 engine layer for Quantum Field Theory: triadic-substrate integration, multi-regime simulation hooks, excitation-resonance mapping, and hybrid-canon scaffolding.

engine.description: Integrates QFT into the triadic substrate, enabling multi-regime reasoning, excitation propagation, and hybrid-canon simulation.

mapping.structure: Excitations correspond to resonance modes in the substrate; fields encode coherence grammars.
mapping.behavior: Propagation emerges from resonance alignment across substrate channels.
mapping.symmetry: Symmetry generators correspond to substrate invariants shaping excitation stability.

constraints: Propagation speed and locality are substrate invariants within regime.

R1.behavior: Excitations lose meaning; resonance collapses to primitive interactions.
R1.notes: No stable operator algebra; coherence too weak.

R2.behavior: Local excitations and propagators behave coherently; symmetry structure emerges.

R3.behavior: Full interaction grammar; stable excitation spectra and renormalized coherence.

R4.behavior: Effective field behavior; large-scale symmetry-driven resonance.

hooks.name: excitation_resonance_sim
hooks.description: Simulates excitations as resonance modes shaped by symmetry and interaction structure.

hooks.name: propagator_resonance_sim
hooks.description: Models propagation as resonance alignment across substrate channels.

hooks.name: renormalization_flow_sim
hooks.description: Simulates coherence repair across energy scales.

hooks.name: regime_transition_sim
hooks.description: Simulates breakdown of QFT coherence across R1→R2→R3→R4 transitions.

simulation.notes: Simulations operate on resonance patterns and substrate invariants, not on fields as physical substances.

hybrid_canon.purpose: Enable agentic AIs to reason across quantum, relativistic, and informational modules using shared substrate invariants.
